liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Alabama Getaway** (2 reviews): Opening duo featured fiery soloing and solid vocals, starting the set with high energy; Jerry blew lyrics, and the band likely shelved the song after 1985 [24][27]
- **I Ain't Superstitious** (1 review): The transition to Down In The Bottom kept the original Minglewood time signature [27]
- **Space** (1 review): Reviewer disputes claim that Jerry teased St. Stephen notes during the eight-minute Space jam [19]

## The recordings

- **gd1985-03-21.163330.akg451.neumann.u87.blend.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 22 songs; 142 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1985-03-21.176003.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 140 min [2]
- **gd1985-03-21.167348.senn441.hunt.mattes.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 141 min [4]
- **gd1985-03-21.senn421.mccue.ford.33949.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 23 songs; 137 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [7]
- **gd1985-03-21.nak300.damico.87046.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 137 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [9]. Said about its sound: Reviewer notes the large coliseum acoustics cause sound to bounce, aiding immersion in jams [21]

## Around the show

- Reviewer traveled from the Bronx to Hampton, contrasting the gritty city with Virginia [18]
- Crowd loved Bobby's screeching and stuttering vocals, though the reviewer finds them inauthentic [26]
- Reviewer rates this show's performances of key songs stronger than those in Providence and Irvine [22]
- Reviewer rates this show's performances of key songs stronger than those in Providence and Irvine [23]
- Reviewer argues March 1985 shows are often overlooked compared to the attention June receives [24]
- Reviewer notes these Hampton shows are largely overlooked in hindsight, despite being excellent [25]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1985-03-21.163330.akg451.neumann.u87.blend.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Rob Eaton; transferred by Rob, Eaton, Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Rob Eaton's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; (2) AKG 451's w/ CK8 shotguns (Left + Right) + (1)Neumann U87 (Center) blend > Nakamichi 550 [1]. Also: Rob Eaton recorded and transferred; Joe D'Amico's Nakamichi 300 patched Drums and Other One [1]
- **gd1985-03-21.176003.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Michael Hessberg; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Michael Hessberg's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser ME-80 mics > Sony D5M [2]
- **gd1985-03-21.167348.senn441.hunt.mattes.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Rob Hunt, Ted Mattes; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Rob Hunt and Ted Mattes' Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 441 mics > Sony D5M [4]
- **gd1985-03-21.senn421.mccue.ford.33949.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Mark McCue, Adam, Monica & John; transferred by Alex Ford; source: (FOB) 2 Sennheiser421's > Sony TC-D5 > TDK MA90 (Set I) TDK MA-R90 [aluminum core (Set II)]. [7]. Also: Bob's vocal mic cuts in at 0:44; microphones on T-Bar, chest high, front of band [7]
- **gd1985-03-21.nak300.damico.87046.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Joe D'Amico; transferred by Joe D'Amico; source: nak 300 mics > sony d5 > MAC [9]
